entities.name: Echembrotus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Echembrotus was an Arcadian Greek lyric poet of the Archaic period, known chiefly from Pausanias’ report that he dedicated a bronze tripod to Heracles after a victory associated with the early Pythian contests. His name thus sits at the intersection of lyric performance, Panhellenic competition, and dedicatory religion in archaic Greece.

Almost nothing of his verse survives; he is a testimonial figure rather than a readable author. Yet the notice matters for reconstructing how local Arcadian talent entered wider Hellenic festival circuits as Delphi’s prestige grew.

In literary history Echembrotus exemplifies the many archaic poets remembered by a single anecdote—evidence of a competitive song culture whose texts largely vanished while dedications and travel stories remained.
